prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate objective function for a GNN-based netlist tier-partitioner (2-tier 3D IC).
Hypothesis of the change: The baseline product-form cut already gives the lowest crit_cross of all evaluated candidates; the parent's additive critical-pair star penalty fights it and inflates crit_cross, so instead I keep the cut/balance/binarisation backbone byte-identical and replace the additive penalty with a *mild multiplicative* reweighting of the cut term by a net-level criticality factor (1 + alpha*mean_crit_of_pins, alpha small, clamped), which can only nudge the cut toward keeping timing-critical nets intact without adding a competing gradient; this should lower crit_cross and crit-weighted cut (both strongly negative rho) and hence TNS.
Rule-based digest (scores are improvement ratios vs. the official baseline; C1..C3 are the training circuits by size):
total=-0.097 robust(mean-std)=-0.133 min_case=-0.166 seed_std=0.131 tns_mean=+0.023 all_valid=True
  C1: score=+0.078 dWNS=+9.7% dTNS=+8.0% per-seed=[+0.09 -0.05 +0.19]
  C2: score=-0.009 dWNS=-1.2% dTNS=-0.8% per-seed=[+0.08 -0.11 +0.00]
  C3: score=-0.166 dWNS=-51.9% dTNS=+1.2% per-seed=[-0.07 -0.46 +0.03]
  partition stats vs baseline:
  C1: cut 137->110, wcut 421->330, crit_cross 0.011->0.005, repair_flips 103->47, changed-vs-baseline 14.6%
  C2: cut 318->310, wcut 1007->976, crit_cross 0.000->0.000, repair_flips 238->231, changed-vs-baseline 6.2%
  C3: cut 582->586, wcut 1955->1957, crit_cross 0.069->0.058, repair_flips 353->361, changed-vs-baseline 5.5%
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID, first classify the failure (crash / non-finite loss / balance repair failure / timeout) and whether it is systematic or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which circuit/metric moved and the plausible mechanism (cut nets, critical-pair cross-tier, repair flips)? (3) is the seed spread acceptable? (4) one concrete next step. No preamble.

response:
(1) Partially: crit_cross fell on C1 (0.011→0.005) and C3 (0.069→0.058) with lower wcut, but C3 dWNS collapsed (-51.9%) and total/robust are negative, so the mild reweighting did not translate to TNS gains.

(2) C1 improved broadly (cut 137→110, repair_flips 103→47); C3 cut/wcut barely moved yet crit_cross dropped—suggesting the factor nudged critical nets without reducing total crossings, and repair flips rose (353→361), plausibly destabilizing timing.

(3) seed_std=0.131 with C3 per-seed [-0.07,-0.46,+0.03] is too wide; not acceptable.

(4) Sweep alpha downward and add a repair-flip guard, validating on C3 seeds.
